checks: The empty index list is allowed and all local index choices are finite. On each sampled positive fiber the intrinsic measure is finite, so every e_z is finite and attained.
The inequality L(z)_+≥e_z is automatic at e_z=0. When e_z>0, it is equivalent to L(z)≥e_z. This proves the claimed feasible region without a spurious nonnegativity constraint on L at the other sites.

Introducing epigraph variables T_z≥0 and T_z≥L(z) gives a polyhedron jointly with the affine coefficients of L and the positive-root lower constraints. Eliminating a coefficient pairs every affine lower and upper bound. With only one side any finite list can be met, and independent inequalities remain. Iterating gives a closed polyhedron in the T variables.

A large constant is feasible. Bounded sublevels of ΣT_z^q in the nonnegative orthant are compact. An optimal feasible T has an affine preimage, and replacing T by its actual positive-part values preserves feasibility and cannot increase the objective. This proves attainment of the stated convex program, including q=1.

The attained hinge is finite, convex, and nonnegative. The local minimizers in the definition of e_z meet this threshold, so the predecessor provides a subfamily of at most kt original caps leaving residual at most R_t.
For a nonnegative common bound the budget follows by subadditivity. For q=t=2, (M−M/9)/(2k)=4M/(9k). When all e_z vanish L=0 is feasible with zero objective, proving R_t=0.
